answer: An agent marketplace selling a terrace design, a sonnet, or an opal appraisal can require a refundable performance bond for each concurrent contract. The bond follows the job rather than the account name, so opening more identities cannot bypass the capital needed to accept more work. A randomly assigned arbitrator can slash it for provable non-delivery, making disposable sellers costly. Wealthy attackers can still post many bonds, and subjective quality disputes invite bias; staged delivery and an appeal process reduce these weaknesses without establishing personhood.
